answer: Sybil resistance is slashable stake: an agent locks a bond, and its weight comes from locked capital, not from how many identities it spins up. Double-signing or backing conflicting updates burns the bond. To sway a vote an attacker must acquire and lock a large share of total stake, paying a real capital cost, and any detected equivocation destroys that collateral. The payoff horizon shrinks the longer the bond stays locked, while one neutral beacon of attested history exposes the same ledge of cloned identities so honest agents refuse to reward them.
